subject: Follow-up: Trial next steps & procurement questions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acme.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Trial next steps & procurement questions

Hi Jordan — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from today's call: 

• Success criteria you mentioned: 1) consistent latency <200ms (p90) for core generative flows, 2) 10k+ tokens/day across the pilot team, and 3) no PII logging in telemetry.
• Trial scope: 4-week pilot starting when you’re ready — we can map billing to the production cutover date or the PO acceptance date (see options below).
• Procurement / commercial path options we discussed:
  - PO to Redwood billing (net 30) — preferred for enterprise buyers.
  - Card payment for faster conversion (self-serve).
  - AWS Marketplace listing for procurement teams that require marketplace billing.

Attachments: trial-summary-acme.pdf (pilot plan + success metrics).

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm procurement preference (PO vs card vs marketplace)?
2) If PO — please share the procurement contact and expected PO timeline (we can provide invoice and tax details).
3) Confirm target start date for billing/paid contract (we tentatively suggested Jul 6 on the call).

I'll loop in Stephanie from billing to expedite any PO paperwork. Happy to align on a DocuSign/contract flow if that helps.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
From: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acme.com>

Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Trial next steps & procurement questions

Thanks Marissa — great recap. A few items from procurement side: 

On Tue, Jun 22, 2026 at 3:10 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Jordan — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from today's call:
>
> • Success criteria you mentioned: 1) consistent latency <200ms (p90) for core generative flows, 2) 10k+ tokens/day across the pilot team, and 3) no PII logging in telemetry.

Procurement here typically requires a PO (net 30). Marketplace billing is preferred when available but not mandatory. If we do PO, typical turnaround is ~10 business days once we have Redwood's invoice information and legal terms (we'll need your W-9 / tax ID).

A couple of clarifying questions: 
• Can billing start be tied to the production cutover date instead of PO receipt? Ideally we'd start billing on the agreed production start (we're aiming for the week of Jul 6).
• Is Redwood listed on AWS Marketplace (we prefer marketplace billing where possible)?
• Who should we address the PO to and what company information do you need?

I'll await the invoice instructions and any MSA you can provide.

—Jordan
Jordan Hayes
Product Lead, Integrations | Acme Corp
jordan.hayes@acme.com | (650) 555-0199

Thanks Jordan — answers below and a couple of action items.

On Tue, Jun 23, 2026 at 9:20 AM Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acme.com> wrote:
> Procurement here typically requires a PO (net 30). Marketplace billing is preferred when available but not mandatory. If we do PO, typical turnaround is ~10 business days once we have Redwood's invoice information and legal terms (we'll need your W-9 / tax ID).
>
> A couple of clarifying questions: 
> • Can billing start be tied to the production cutover date instead of PO receipt? Ideally we'd start billing on the agreed production start (we're aiming for the week of Jul 6).
> • Is Redwood listed on AWS Marketplace (we prefer marketplace billing where possible)?
> • Who should we address the PO to and what company information do you need?

Short answers: yes, yes (we are on AWS Marketplace but not all customers use it), and details below. Longer detail: 

1) Billing start date options (pick one):
  A) Billing begins when we accept the PO (standard).
  B) Billing begins on mutually agreed production cutover date (we can implement this; requires PO to reference the deal and a signed MSA).
  C) If you go through AWS Marketplace, billing is handled by the marketplace provider and start can be aligned to the subscription activation date.

2) Marketplace status: Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace (we have a subscription listing). If Acme prefers that path, procurement will need the AWS subscription listing info — happy to connect your procurement team with our Marketplace PM to speed that up.

3) PO / invoice info to include:
  - Bill to: Redwood Inference, Inc.
  - Address: 123 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94105
  - Tax ID / W-9: 12-3456789 (we will send the official W-9 as an attachment)
  - Please reference Deal ID: ACME-2026-TRIAL-42 on the PO and any accompanying email.

Attachments: redwood-invoice-instructions.pdf (invoice template and required fields), W-9 stub.

Proposed timeline: if Acme can issue a PO by Jul 2 we can align billing to Jul 6 production cutover. If PO comes later, we will set the billing start to PO acceptance date unless you explicitly request the production cutover option and we have a signed MSA.

Action items:
• Jordan / Procurement: share point person and expected PO date.
• Jordan: confirm whether you want to pursue AWS Marketplace path (I can introduce Marketplace PM).
• Marissa/Stephanie: we will prepare an MSA + invoice packet and fast-track once we have procurement contact.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call with procurement if helpful.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
